doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Vaudeville flourishes and vocal impersonations in her act
summary: Her hip shaking and impersonations of Lena Horne, Nellie Lutcher and Billie Holiday break up the monotony; audiences have a limited attention span.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Some of the non-musical flourishes that you incorporate into your act, the hip shaking and all, does that go back to vaudeville influences, not necessarily with you…
It could be. We learned about Chippy Hill and Step ‘n’ Fetchit. Not Step ‘n’ Fetchit, Snake Hips Tucker.

That long tradition of vaudeville performance and entertainers, even going into Armstrong and Dizzy Gillespie, the clowning…tell me about those performance aspects with some of the vocal impersonations, could you tell me about that?
I could do Lena Horne and Ella, not Etta Jones, I keep calling her James sometimes. I can do Nellie Lutcher, Rose Murphy and a lot of them; Billie Holiday, especially.
I assumed the audience really loved that.
It breaks up the monotony of the music.
Tell me about breaking up the monotony of the music, the entertainment role that you also…
People have a retention span—you can’t play too much music. You have to learn how to cut off and cut on.
